nodes.label: Parlour (project overview)
nodes.author: Michael Parker
nodes.rationale: A voice assistant for your home that runs on a Mac you already own. A small local model handles the house; a cloud model steps in only when a question is beyond it and only ever gets the sentence, never the audio. MIT, copyright 2026 Michael Parker.

nodes.label: What happens when you speak (voice pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Wake word (openWakeWord, in process, always local) -> record (energy endpointing, stops on 800 ms of silence) -> speech to text (whisper.cpp small.en, kept warm) -> the model (a local model with tools over the OpenAI API) -> tools (Home Assistant over MCP, timers, search, connectors) -> escalate (Claude when the local model says it is out of its depth) -> text to speech (Kokoro, in process) -> the speakers.

nodes.label: Every stage is a provider behind a small interface
nodes.rationale: Each pipeline stage is a provider chosen by name in a single config file. Built-in choices are the fastest found for Apple silicon; anything else is an npm package away (docs/providers.md).

nodes.label: Cloud escalation: text only, decided per question by the local model
nodes.rationale: Claude is called only when the local model says it is out of its depth, and receives only the sentence that was said, never the audio. Privacy is the design intent: no account, no server in the middle.

nodes.label: Getting started (npm install -g parlour, init, text, start)
nodes.rationale: Requires a Mac with Node 22+ and Homebrew; init fetches ffmpeg, whisper.cpp and the models through brew, asks for the Home Assistant address and token and an optional Anthropic key, writes ~/.config/parlour/config.json and secrets.env, offers to run at login, and finishes with parlour doctor. LM Studio is the easy local model option; anything speaking the OpenAI chat completions API works.

nodes.label: The parlour CLI commands
nodes.rationale: init [--yes] [--no-deps] [--no-service] [--porcelain], start [--events], text, doctor [--json], service install|uninstall|restart|status|logs, connectors add|list|remove, models fetch, config path|show|write|edit, secrets status|set. connectors add signs the household in to a remote MCP server and keeps tokens in the Keychain; the connectors integration is on by default and doctor warns if a hand-written config leaves it out.

nodes.label: parlour doctor
nodes.rationale: Reports which of the moving parts is down, with --json for the app. Run at the end of init. The project's chosen substitute for unit tests on hardware-, model- and network-dependent providers.

nodes.label: One server, any number of rooms (client topology)
nodes.rationale: One machine runs the models, holds the tokens and answers; everything else with a microphone is a client, and the server's own microphone is just one client with no special privileges. Clients: server mic (in process, openWakeWord); satellite (role: satellite, finds the server with Bonjour, holds a socket open, wake word on the server over the stream or locally with localWake); Home Assistant and Voice PE via the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint (wake word on device, HA does STT and speech back); a phone via the page at / with hold-to-talk (thumb as endpoint detector, phone not listening all day); custom hardware via the /listen socket with raw 16 kHz mono PCM; automations via POST /ask.

nodes.label: PARLOUR_TOKEN gates network exposure
nodes.rationale: All clients need PARLOUR_TOKEN. Without it the server only listens on loopback and does not advertise itself over Bonjour, because a voice assistant on an open port can turn the heating on and read your shopping list.

nodes.label: Documentation index (docs/ pages)
nodes.rationale: docs/architecture.md (ports, provider registry, session state machine), docs/providers.md (writing a provider or integration as an npm package), docs/clients.md (satellites, phone page, hardware, /ask, Bonjour), docs/home-assistant.md (MCP Server integration, OpenAI Conversation integration, muting, migration), docs/desktop.md (menu bar app), docs/tuning.md (false wakes), docs/wake-word.md (training your own wake word).

nodes.label: Repository layout (packages/parlour, apps/desktop, apps/site, docs)
nodes.rationale: packages/parlour is the npm package (core, built-in providers, integrations, server, CLI); apps/desktop is the menu bar app (Tauri, React, a Rust shell that drives the CLI); apps/site is one page and one stylesheet; docs/ holds the pages. pnpm and nx; pnpm check runs typecheck, lint and tests across every project.

nodes.label: What Parlour does not do, on purpose
nodes.rationale: Does not tell voices apart (everyone is the same user). Does not cancel its own echo, which is why barge-in is off by default. Does not fail over: one server, satellites wait for it rather than electing a new one, because a house with two brains that disagree is worse than a house with none. No per-person connectors: tokens belong to the household because a satellite cannot tell who is talking. No Linux yet: service manager, secret store and audio sit behind interfaces so it is a contribution rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: openWakeWord (wake word engine)
nodes.rationale: In-process, always-local wake word detection on the Mac; runs on onnxruntime.

nodes.label: whisper.cpp (speech to text)
nodes.rationale: small.en model kept warm on the machine (io.parlour.whisper LaunchAgent) so transcription finishes in under a second.

nodes.label: Kokoro (text to speech)
nodes.rationale: In-process voice on the Mac; speaks the first sentence while the rest is still being generated.

nodes.label: LM Studio (local model server)
nodes.rationale: The easy option for the local model; init offers to install it. Anything that speaks the OpenAI chat completions API works too.

nodes.label: Home Assistant over MCP
nodes.rationale: Home Assistant's MCP Server integration publishes whatever is exposed to voice assistants as tools, so Parlour can do exactly what is allowed and nothing more. The OpenAI Conversation integration pointed at Parlour's /v1 lets Voice PE satellites use it as their brain.
